content.comment_body: Hello [product_name] users, I've attached a .lld file showing my issue. At first glance, it looks like an empty ladder program, but when trying to download to the device, the compiler reports unconnected blocks. In the simulator, it's possible to simulate Q12 even though it's not used in the program. My question is: how do I remove these blocks? I prefer not to switch to FBD view because it causes confusion. Best regards [user_name]
Hi, If you have the latest version, the only way I know is to switch to FBD view, remove the blocks, and then switch back to Ladder.
But if I do that, the program becomes very messy.
Hello, It's already quite messy since you can't download it. Switching to FBD and then back to Ladder is the only option. I'm curious—did this happen due to copying and pasting blocks? Regards,

It's frustrating to hear that a software bug likely cost me a whole day. I'm using [product_name] Soft Comfort version 7. This issue occurred simply: I added a Q12 contact, but there was no Q12 coil available to add, so I removed the Q12 contact. However, the compiler still sees Q12.
Hello, This situation can happen when copying and pasting networks. If the network can't be copied, the program adds a block and connects it to a lower block (visible in FBD, not in Ladder).
A new question by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread titled 'How do I use simulator in master to master network program?' Best regards Min_Moderator

analysis.insight_summary: Users face issues with invisible blocks in ladder diagrams when using [product_name] Soft Comfort, especially after copying/pasting or deleting elements. This results in errors during compilation and simulation, where ladder diagrams look empty, but the compiler detects unconnected blocks and outputs such as Q12 remain simulatable despite being seemingly unused. The main workaround is switching to FBD view to delete problematic blocks, but many find this process cumbersome and undesirable. There is notable frustration over what is considered a software defect.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to remove unused or hidden blocks directly within the ladder view, without needing to switch to FBD, and want to prevent hidden items that cause program errors or simulate unexpected outputs.
